title: Model selection seatbelt wires and copy — sprint notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick capture of the low-fidelity wireframes and microcopy experiments for the Model Selection 'seatbelt' pattern — a set of UI constraints and callouts to prevent accidental or risky model-version pinning when creating endpoints.

Context / problem statement:
- Engineers frequently pin model versions at endpoint creation and later discover regressions (quality or latency).
- We need an intermediate affordance during onboarding/wizard that nudges the user to think about rollback, fallback, and test traffic split.
- Aim: reduce high-cost mistakes while keeping fast path for experienced users.

Design hypothesis:
1) Introduce a compact ‘seatbelt’ strip in the endpoint creation flow (below model picker) that summarizes pin impact and lets you choose safety options: soft-pin, hard-pin, or staged-rollout.
2) Provide targeted microcopy for each option to reduce ambiguity.
3) Add an inline test traffic toggle with quick 'smoke test' checklist and an automated canary route suggestion.

Wireframe notes (low-fi):
- Screen A: Catalog list (left pane) / Model card grid (center) / Detail & selection (right drawer). Selecting a model opens the drawer with version dropdown and the seatbelt strip below.
- Seatbelt strip (horizontal): left: chosen model + version chip. middle: risk badge (green/yellow/red) derived from perf/quality profile. right: primary CTA (Select & Continue) plus an overflow chevron for safety settings.
- Safety settings panel (drawer): radio buttons: Soft pin (default), Hard pin (locks version), Staged rollout (percentage slider + schedule). Below radios: small 'Why this matters' paragraph and link to rollout best practices.

Microcopy candidates (short):
- Seatbelt label: "Confirm model version"
- Risk badge tooltip: "Estimated risk: based on recent evals, latency profile, and regen score."
- Soft pin description: "Prefer this model but allow automatic fallback to compatible variants if regressions occur."
- Hard pin description: "Lock this exact model version; no automatic fallback. Use for strict reproducibility."
- Staged rollout label: "Gradual rollout" / subcopy: "Start at 5% and monitor quality metrics before increasing."
- Smoke test CTA: "Run quick smoke test" -> modal copy: "Send 10 test requests now — we’ll report success/failure and latency distribution."
- Confirmation when hard-pin chosen: Title: "Lock model version?" Body: "Hard pins prevent automated fallbacks. To proceed, type the endpoint name to confirm." Button: "Lock & Create"

Error & edge cases: 
- If selected version is deprecated: banner in strip: "This version is deprecated — last validated 2025-09-12." CTA: "Pick latest compatible"
- If autopromote is configured and user picks hard-pin: inline warning: "Auto-promote disabled for this endpoint while pinned."
- Conflicting pins across routes: tooltip: "Route-level pin overrides endpoint-level pin." (needs product decision)

Accessibility notes:
- Seatbelt strip must be keyboard-focusable and have aria-describedby linking to the risk badge tooltip and the smoke-test button.
- Slider for staged rollout should support numeric input and readable labels for screen readers.

Telemetry & guardrails (implementation hooks):
- Track: selection method (catalog vs search), chosen safety option, whether smoke-test was run, time-to-create after selecting version.
- Emit event when user chooses hard-pin so SRE/ops can review spikes in support tickets.

Backlog grooming (short tasks & owners):
- PROD-827: Implement seatbelt UI skeleton (owner: Diego Ramos)
- PROD-829: Add risk badge scoring pipeline (owner: Maya Chen)
- ENG-1423: Hook smoke-test runner into test infra and report schema (owner: Samir Patel)
- UX-410: Microcopy iteration + localization strings (owner: Arielle Park)
- QA-66: Test keyboard and screen-reader flows for seatbelt (owner: QA team)

Open questions for next sync:
- Do we treat 'soft pin' as a non-binding hint for the routing layer, or should it only enable fallback logic?
- What threshold should the risk badge use to classify a version as 'red'? (perf delta vs eval regressions)
- How to represent multi-model endpoints (ensemble) in the seatbelt?

Next steps (this sprint):
- Wireframe polish: convert to Figma frames (Arielle) by 2026-03-14.
- Proto: dev brings up skeleton in staging to capture telemetry (Diego + Samir) by 2026-03-22.
- Copy pass: finalize confirmation modal language and error banners (Arielle) by 2026-03-18.

Notes-to-self / scribbles: 
- Keep the fast-path at one click for teams who already have a pinned default. Seatbelt should be collapsible with a 'don’t show again' remembered per-user.
- Consider adding a lightweight explainer tour for first 3 endpoint creations (product ask).

Related links: Confluence design brief (linked_artifacts above), initial research notes: slack thread #console-onboard: /thread/8432, sample telemetry schema GH-1459.

End.
